name: Vantage
title: Coded prototypes are easy to build now — and weirdly hard to share.
tagline: A private, revocable way to share a coded prototype with the exact people you choose — and see how they actually use it.

heroMedia.alt: The Vantage console — issuing one personal link per person, then reading usability results

intro: You've built a coded prototype and want to show it to five specific people. Sending the HTML, screen sharing, Vercel, chat artifacts and Figma plugins all fall short. A staff designer, Michał Krzton, posted exactly this problem — it had 42 comments twelve hours later — and a conversation with designer Adrian Mendoza about how AI is changing our workflows got me curious enough to build the answer.

Vantage lets you share a coded prototype securely with the people you choose. Each person gets a personal link you can revoke, and if you set up a usability test you get tasks, feedback and results back. It runs as one Node process with no third-party packages, so a security team can read every line.

sections.label: How I used AI
sections.heading: Building it was the fast part
body: Claude Code had a working version running over a weekend. I didn't want to put my name on code I couldn't vouch for, so once it worked I stopped adding things and started reading.

I asked Claude to go through its own code the way four different people would: a staff engineer, a security reviewer, a privacy officer and an engineering director. The first pass turned up nineteen issues, two of them serious. I fixed seventeen that day. Then I went through the whole thing again, line by line, and found thirty more. I'm not proud of the count. I am glad I could read the code well enough to find them.

sections.label: Where I overrode it
sections.heading: The calls it didn't make on its own
body: It suggested a watermark to stop screenshots. A watermark doesn't stop a screenshot. I took it out and wrote down plainly what the tool can't do.

On security it wrote the dangerous defaults up as warnings in a doc. I changed them so you can't get them wrong: the server won't start with open sign-in unless you switch it on deliberately, and a hosted bill can't go above zero. And twice, when it handed me a screenshot or a made-up version of a real interface, I sent it back and asked for the real thing.

reflection.label: Honest status
reflection.heading: It's not done, and I'm still finding out if it's the right answer
body: Nobody but me has used Vantage yet, so this is intent, not evidence. I made it open source to learn from people who know more than I do — if you've hit this same wall, or you think I'm solving the wrong problem, I want to hear it.
